reference.source: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation / Nelson Textbook of Pediatrics
clinicalPearls: Characterised by congenital dislocations of large joints, notably bilateral knee dislocations, together with hip and elbow dislocations and severe talipes
The dominant form is caused by variants in FLNB encoding filamin B, a cytoskeletal protein regulating chondrocyte function; rarer recessive Larsen-like phenotypes have distinct causes
A characteristic flat facial appearance with a depressed nasal bridge, prominent forehead, and widely spaced eyes aids recognition
Hand findings include cylindrical, spatulate fingers and, radiographically, an accessory carpal ossification centre
Cervical spine abnormalities with kyphosis and instability are a critical hazard that can cause myelopathy and complicate airway management
Additional features may include cleft palate, hearing loss, and, in some, cardiac and respiratory (tracheomalacia) involvement
Diagnosis integrates the pattern of congenital joint dislocations and facial features with FLNB molecular testing
reference.pathophysiology: Larsen syndrome most often results from dominant variants in FLNB, which encodes filamin B, a cytoskeletal protein that cross-links actin and regulates signalling and mechanical responses in chondrocytes. Disturbed filamin B function alters chondrocyte proliferation and differentiation and the development of joints, ligaments, and the vertebral column. This produces the hallmark congenital large-joint dislocations, ligamentous laxity, cervical spine anomalies, and characteristic craniofacial and hand features. FLNB variants underlie a spectrum of skeletal disorders ranging from Larsen syndrome to more severe atelosteogenesis phenotypes.
additionalInvestigations: Skeletal survey documenting joint dislocations, accessory carpal ossification, and spinal anomalies
Cervical spine imaging including flexion-extension views to assess kyphosis and instability
FLNB molecular genetic testing to confirm the diagnosis
Airway and respiratory assessment for tracheomalacia before anaesthesia
Echocardiography where cardiac involvement is suspected
redFlags: Cervical kyphosis or instability with myelopathy, particularly around anaesthesia
Airway compromise from tracheomalacia or cervical involvement
Neurological deterioration from spinal cord compression
reference.prognosis: With careful orthopaedic and spinal management, intelligence and lifespan are generally normal, but untreated cervical instability can cause devastating neurological injury, and joint dislocations and foot deformity require staged surgical and physiotherapy management.
pitfalls: Overlooking cervical kyphosis and instability, risking cord injury during airway management
Reducing knee or hip dislocations without recognising the underlying syndrome and its spinal risks
Failing to assess for tracheomalacia before anaesthesia
Confusing it with arthrogryposis without appropriate radiographic and genetic evaluation
references: Smith's Recognizable Patterns of Human Malformation
management: No disease-modifying drug exists; the mainstay is staged orthopaedic reduction and surgical stabilisation of the congenital large-joint dislocations (bilateral knees, hips, elbows) with serial casting and soft-tissue release for talipes
Protect and stabilise the cervical spine, bracing or surgically fusing cervical kyphosis and instability to prevent myelopathy from cord compression
Plan every anaesthetic as a difficult airway, anticipating cervical instability and tracheomalacia, using fibreoptic and cervical-protection techniques
Provide supportive physiotherapy and orthotics to maintain joint function, with cleft palate repair and hearing amplification for sensorineural loss
Undertake surveillance with serial flexion-extension cervical imaging, echocardiography where cardiac involvement is suspected, and periodic audiology
Coordinate care across clinical genetics, orthopaedic and spinal surgery, ENT, anaesthesia, and cardiology
Offer genetic counselling for the autosomal dominant FLNB inheritance and screen at-risk relatives
